lane.name: Emo and Midwest emo
lane.definition: Cap'n Jazz, American Football, Modern Baseball: the emo line from which C9 borrows.

albums.label: Sub Pop
albums.description: The foundational second-wave emo album, pairing Jeremy Enigk's keening, cracked voice with dense, dynamic guitar builds on a Seattle grunge-era Sub Pop roster. Widely cited as the record that turned hardcore-adjacent emo into something melodic and anthemic.
albums.lineage: Emerges from the Sub Pop/Seattle underground-rock world of V16's college-rock lineage and launches the emo line (X6) that seems, by way of American Football and the emo revival, to feed the twangy crossover of Core's C9.

albums.label: Man With Gun
albums.description: The chaotic, herky-jerky debut and only proper studio album from a band central to Midwest emo, all yelped vocals, start-stop math-rock riffing and teenage overspill. Tim Kinsella, his brother Mike and future Promise Ring member Davey von Bohlen all pass through here.
albums.lineage: Sounds like an offshoot of the American underground/college-rock noise of V16 and the punk foundation of X14; through shared members it directly opens the line to American Football and Joan of Arc and, later, the 2010s emo revival rather than Core twang.

albums.label: Crank!
albums.description: A Texas emo landmark of quiet-loud dynamics and raw, cracked-voice catharsis, considered alongside Diary as a genre-defining second-wave emo record despite the band's short lifespan.
albums.lineage: Sounds of a piece with Sunny Day Real Estate in the second-wave emo line growing out of V16's underground rock scene, pointing toward the 2000s emo mainstream rather than the Core.

albums.label: Jade Tree
albums.description: A Milwaukee band's shift from post-hardcore into jangly, hooky pop-emo, with Davey von Bohlen's lisped, boyish vocals over bright major-key guitars. A key bridge between hardcore-rooted emo and the pop-punk-adjacent emo of the early 2000s.
albums.lineage: Sounds grown from the Midwest hardcore scene near X14 into the jangly, pop-facing wing of X6, pointing toward 2000s pop-emo and Modern Baseball-style revival bands rather than the Core.

albums.label: Polyvinyl
albums.description: Mike Kinsella's post-Cap'n Jazz project distilled Midwest emo into gentle, jazzy guitar interplay, trumpet and conversational vocals. Its lone original-era album became the genre's defining text, endlessly cited by 2010s emo-revival bands.
albums.lineage: A direct offshoot of Cap'n Jazz within X6 through Mike Kinsella, trading noise for math-rock jangle; the sound it codified seems to feed both later Midwest emo bands and the twangy emo crossover of Core lane C9.

albums.label: Triple Crown
albums.description: Evan Weiss's first proper full-length as Into It. Over It., a full-band Midwest-emo-revival guitar record that sounds indebted to American Football and Cap'n Jazz. It works as a connector between the original Midwest emo sound and its 2010s revival, with twinkly guitars and conversational, wordy vocals.
albums.lineage: Carries the American Football math-rock jangle forward into the 2010s emo revival within X6, part of the same scene that overlaps with Core's C9.

albums.label: Run for Cover
albums.description: A Philadelphia band's breakout emo-revival record, all conversational, self-deprecating lyrics and twin-vocalist trade-offs over fast, hooky guitar pop. A defining document of the mid-2010s emo revival's college-scene sound.
albums.lineage: Sounds like a 2010s emo-revival descendant of the American Football/Promise Ring lineage within X6, part of the same wave that seems to feed the twangy emo crossover of Core lane C9.

albums.label: Tiny Engines
albums.description: A Massachusetts emo-revival landmark that pairs post-hardcore intensity with raw, therapy-session lyricism about grief and mental illness. Christian Holden's strained, cracking vocals and surging guitars make it the revival's most emotionally direct record.
albums.lineage: Another 2010s branch of the emo-revival wave within X6 that sounds indebted to Sunny Day Real Estate's dynamics, part of the same scene that overlaps with Core's twangy-emo crossover lane C9.
